title: Jan Sahas Social Empowerment Society: JSSES | Studio 1947
description: How Studio 1947 designed and built a new website for JSSES to share its mental health, women's livelihood and migrant resilience work across Madhya Pradesh.
ogTitle: Jan Sahas Social Empowerment Society: JSSES | Studio 1947
ogDescription: How Studio 1947 built a new website for Jan Sahas Social Empowerment Society to grow its community work across Madhya Pradesh.
headline: Jan Sahas Website

hero.alt: Community members photographed for the Jan Sahas Social Empowerment Society website hero

body: Marginalised communities across Madhya Pradesh face linked barriers: little access to mental health support, the stigma around asking for help, gender-based violence, and the insecurity of migrant livelihoods. Jan Sahas Social Empowerment Society (JSSES), set up in 2006, works where these challenges meet. It supports underserved communities through mental health services, women's livelihoods, and migrant resilience programs.

Studio 1947 worked with JSSES to design and build a new website that turns nearly two decades of grassroots work into a clear, trustworthy online presence. One that serves survivors, rural women, migrant workers, donors, and government partners alike.

sections.label: The Mission
body: JSSES works towards a society that is socially, economically, and educationally empowered, where everyone enjoys equal rights and opportunities. Its programs span mental health support, women's livelihood work like the Usha Silai School Program, and the Migrant Resilience Collaborative Program, which supports safe and dignified migration.

sections.label: The Challenge
body: An NGO's website is often the first point of contact for survivors seeking help, donors weighing a cause, and government partners checking credibility. JSSES needed a site that could do three things at once:

cards.title: Build Trust & Credibility
cards.body: Present nearly two decades of grassroots work with the confidence that attracts donors, CSR partners, and government collaborations.

cards.title: Make Help Accessible
cards.body: Give survivors and community members a clear, stigma-free path to counselling, legal support, and program information, in simple, human language.

cards.title: Showcase Program Impact
cards.body: Show the depth of mental health outreach, women's livelihoods, and migrant resilience work with honest, evidence-backed storytelling.

sections.heading: Community-Led Programs, Clearly Told
sections.label: Program Structure
body: The site is built around JSSES's core programs. Each one is presented with its approach, services, and measurable outcomes, so visitors quickly understand how the organisation works on the ground:

cards.title: Community Mental Health Support
cards.body: A mental health model with many partners: counselling centres across several districts, run by psychologists, social workers, and trained barefoot counsellors, plus frontline training and community awareness.

cards.title: Usha Silai School Program
cards.body: A nationwide nine-day module that teaches women sewing, machine repair, and life skills, so they can run their own small businesses, and link 2,000 women to employment.

cards.title: Migrant Resilience Collaborative
cards.body: Social security access, worker protection, and safe mobility support for migrant workers, from the Resilience Connect app and a toll-free helpline to legal aid and government scheme registration.

sections.label: Referrals From Law Enforcement
body: One achievement stands out in the site's story. JSSES has built strong working relationships with the Women's Police and Juvenile Police, who now refer cases that need mental health counselling, fact-finding in sensitive situations, and legal support. The website gives this collaboration, and the trust behind it, the visibility it deserves.

sections.heading: Build & Interface Design
sections.label: Build & Technology
body: To make the site fast, reliable, and easy to maintain, Studio 1947 built it as a modern Next.js app with a component-based interface. It is made for quick page loads on rural mobile connections, clear navigation, and simple content updates by the JSSES team.

The design leans on a deep midnight indigo drawn from the organisation's own identity, paired with generous white space and easy-to-read type. The site feels calm, credible, and human, never clinical.

sections.label: Page-by-Page
body: Each section of the site moves visitors from curiosity to confidence. It starts with the programs, then the evidence, the people, and finally a clear invitation to act.

cards.title: Program-First Structure
cards.body: Mental health, livelihoods, and migration each get their own story, from mission and approach to services, impact data, and how to get help.

cards.title: Board & Governance Transparency
cards.body: A board-members section profiles the leadership (legal professionals, survivor leaders, and community advocates), building trust at a glance.

cards.title: Resources, Reports & Media Hub
cards.body: Annual reports (FY 2023 to 24 and 2024 to 25), mental health resources, event coverage, and photo galleries, so donors, journalists, and partners can check and share the organisation's ongoing work.

cards.title: Clear Pathways to Get Involved
cards.body: Simple, separate routes for donating through a secure online payment gateway, volunteering, or applying for open roles, each with its own call-to-action.

sections.heading: Client Impact & Outcomes
sections.label: Measuring Success
list: A Website That Matches the Mission: One calm, credible site that presents mental health, women's livelihoods, and migrant resilience work with the dignity they deserve.
Stronger Trust: Clear governance, program approach, and published reports and resources that support CSR engagement, donor confidence, and government partnerships.
Easier Paths to Help: Survivors and community members can now find counselling, legal support, and program information (including the police referral network) in one stigma-free place.
